projects.name: VetAssist AI
projects.description: A guarded LangGraph workflow for veterinarians, moving case work through symptoms, test suggestions, result analysis, differential diagnosis, and treatment planning with evidence validation.

details.problem: Clinical workflows need ordered reasoning and verified evidence, not an open-ended chatbot that jumps straight to treatment.
approach: LangGraph phase guards keep the clinician inside the correct case sequence.
Recommendations pass SOP, literature, and LLM reasoning checks before display.
Redis and MongoDB snapshots allow safe backward navigation through a case.

architecture.label: Phase graph
architecture.detail: State machine with guarded clinical progression.

architecture.label: Evidence chain
architecture.detail: SOP match, literature lookup, and bounded model reasoning.

architecture.label: Validated output
architecture.detail: Recommendation returned with support and confidence.

outcomes: Doctors can move backward without corrupting state.

projects.name: Pawspector AI
projects.description: A multi-graph triage assistant that routes free text and photos into specialized conversation graphs, with memory layers for resumable multi-pet sessions.

details.problem: Pet owners provide messy descriptions, partial context, and images. Keyword bots collapse under that variety.
approach: A lightweight router chooses the right graph for text-first, photo-first, utility, or species-mismatch messages.
GPT-4o extracts symptoms and asks dynamic follow-up questions.
A three-layer memory stack prevents repeated model calls on returning sessions.

architecture.label: Specialized graph
architecture.detail: One focused graph handles the message shape.

architecture.label: Triage outcome
architecture.detail: Structured next step for the owner.

outcomes: Photo and text triage share one memory system.

projects.name: Self-Healing CI/CD
projects.description: A CI/CD incident system that classifies failures, runs evidence-based root cause analysis, and gates all remediation through deterministic policy.

details.problem: Repetitive build and runtime failures waste engineering time, but an autonomous fixer needs strong boundaries before it can be trusted.
approach: Rules-first classification handles common CI, Kubernetes, and live-site incidents.
A policy table assigns risk; the model never decides its own authority.
Low-risk remediations auto-run, while risky changes wait for approval.

architecture.label: Signal
architecture.detail: CI, pod, or live-site alert arrives.

architecture.label: Policy
architecture.detail: Deterministic risk gate chooses auto or approval.

outcomes: Safe fixes can run without waiting.
The same incident pipeline handles multiple signal sources.
